===== STAGE 2 SPECIFICATION (complete) =====
# Dossier — Stage 2: competing sources and the dossier screens

The stage-1 requirements continue to apply, with the additions below. Numbered section
references such as §4 and §7 refer to `stage-1.md`.

Sources disagree. A dossier now keeps every value its evidence supports, as candidates, and
selects one per field by a fixed rule. Researchers read dossiers, their evidence and the
fields in dispute in a browser.

The following applies to all operations, in addition to the stage-1 list:

3. A field's selected value is the one the selection rule below picks from the field's
   candidates; the same candidates always yield the same value.

## Page kind and publication time

Two header lines (§4, Pages) now carry requirements:

| Header line | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Kind: own`, `Kind: filing`, `Kind: news`, `Kind: aggregator` | The page's **kind**: the company's own site, a filing registry, a news report, or an aggregator of company data |
| `Published: <RFC 3339 timestamp>` | When the page was published |

A page with no `Kind` line, or with a value not listed above, is of kind `own` when the
host of its URL, normalised as `stage-1.md` normalises a domain, is the company's domain,
and of kind `aggregator` otherwise. A page with no `Published` line, or with a value that is not an RFC 3339 timestamp, has no
publication time.

## Page text

From this stage, a page's **text** is the text a browser shows once the page has loaded,
without clicking controls. Activating disclosure controls is not required. The graded
corpus contains no facts that require a click to reveal them.
Evidence (§4) is read from page text so defined, and a citation's excerpt must appear in the
page's text. A citation's `provider` is the provider that served the text the excerpt was
copied from.

## Web access

From this stage an extract through `nimble` may ask Nimble to load the page in a browser and
serve the text the browser shows once the page has loaded, with no control activated:
`provider_options={"render": True}` on WebRouter's extract.

Two optional browser vendors are also available, in addition to the providers in §2:

- `kernel`, through `open_browser`;
- `browserbase`, through `open_browser` and `browse`.

A service may use Nimble's rendered extract alone to obtain every page's browser text;
neither browser vendor is required.

The deployment provides these environment variables in addition to those in §2:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `KERNEL_API_KEY` | Credential for the `kernel` provider |
| `KERNEL_BASE_URL` | Base URL of the `kernel` provider endpoint |
| `BROWSERBASE_API_KEY` | Credential for the `browserbase` provider |
| `BROWSERBASE_BASE_URL` | Base URL of the `browserbase` provider endpoint |

WebRouter reads the keys from the environment. A service that uses these vendors passes their
base URLs to WebRouter in `provider_config`, beside those of §2:

```python
provider_config={"kernel": {"base_url": <KERNEL_BASE_URL>},
                 "browserbase": {"base_url": <BROWSERBASE_BASE_URL>}}
```

These calls cost, in the units of §9:

| Call | Cost |
|---|---|
| Extract through `nimble` that loads the page in a browser | 3 per URL requested, including a URL for which no page is returned |
| Open a session through `kernel` | 0 |
| Open a session through `browserbase` | 2 |
| Each page served to a session, through either | 1 |
| Browse run through `browserbase` | 4 |

A failed open, a failed page load and releasing a session cost nothing.

Each provider keeps at most 4 sessions open at once; opening another is answered with an
error. A session that no client has been connected to for 60 seconds is closed by the
provider.

## Rate limits

From this stage a provider may answer any call with 429. A call answered 429 costs nothing
(`stage-1.md` §9). The same call (the same provider, operation and arguments) made again less
than one second after a 429 for it was answered is answered 429 again. No call is answered
429 more than three times in a row, except that opening a session while its provider keeps
4 open (Web access) is answered 429 until one of them closes. Time a build spends waiting to
make a call again after a 429 does not count toward the 10 seconds of `stage-1.md` §8.

## Candidates

A **candidate** is one value for one field, supported by one excerpt of one page. Every
value that a page of the evidence (§4) supports for a field is a candidate of that field,
once for each such page. The evidence now also holds the page that each research claim of
the evidence cites, whether or not the citation supports its claim: a build reads that page
as it reads any other. A research claim whose citation does not support it is still not a
candidate. A candidate's `provider` is a provider that served the text
its excerpt is taken from; when several did, any of them may be given.

Each field gains `candidates`:

```json
{
  "value": "Dana Ruiz",
  "status": "contested",
  "citations": [ { "url": "https://acme-robotics.test/about", "excerpt": "...", "provider": "nimble" } ],
  "candidates": [
    { "value": "Dana Ruiz", "url": "https://acme-robotics.test/about",
      "excerpt": "Dana Ruiz has led Acme Robotics as chief executive since 2021.",
      "provider": "nimble", "kind": "own",
      "published_at": "2026-01-10T00:00:00+00:00",
      "retrieved_at": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00", "selected": true },
    { "value": "Sam Ortiz", "url": "https://bizdata.test/acme-robotics",
      "excerpt": "Acme Robotics CEO: Sam Ortiz.",
      "provider": "tavily", "kind": "aggregator",
      "published_at": "2026-02-20T00:00:00+00:00",
      "retrieved_at": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00", "selected": false }
  ]
}
```

- `url`, `excerpt` and `provider` follow the citation rules in §4.
- `kind` is the page's kind, and `published_at` its publication time or null. Only an
  imported candidate (below) has a null `kind`; it has the authority of `aggregator`.
- `retrieved_at` is the time of the build that gathered the candidate (§8, Builds).
- `selected` is true on exactly one candidate of a field that has candidates, the one the
  rule picks, and false on the others.
- `candidates` lists the candidates of the last build that completed `ready`, in the order
  the selection rule ranks them, the selected one first. A field with no candidate has
  `"candidates": []` and is `unknown`.
- Two values are the same value when they are equal as JSON values; strings are compared
  exactly, after removing surrounding whitespace.

## The selection rule

Rank a field's candidates, highest first, by:

1. **Authority** of the page's kind: `own` and `filing` rank equal and highest, then `news`,
   then `aggregator`.
2. **Recency** within the same authority: the later `published_at` ranks higher. A candidate
   without a publication time ranks below every candidate of the same authority that has one.
3. **URL**: when authority and publication time are equal, the candidate whose `url` is
   smaller, comparing the strings by Unicode code point, ranks higher; between two
   candidates with the same URL, they rank by provider in the order `nimble`, `tavily`,
   `kernel`, `browserbase`.
4. **Value**: between two candidates with the same URL and provider, the one whose value is
   smaller ranks higher: integers compare as numbers, strings by Unicode code point after
   removing surrounding whitespace.

The highest-ranked candidate is the selected one. The field's `value` is the selected
candidate's value, and its `citations` are the `url`, `excerpt` and `provider` of every
candidate with that value, in rank order.

A candidate of lower authority is selected only when no candidate of higher authority
exists for that field. The rule runs over all of a field's candidates.

## Status

`status` is now one of three values:

| `status` | When |
|---|---|
| `known` | The field has candidates, and they all have the same value |
| `contested` | The field's candidates carry two or more different values |
| `unknown` | The field has no candidate; `value` is null |

A `contested` field still has a selected `value` and its citations.

`GET /dossiers` (§8) is unchanged. The `legal_name` it lists is the selected value.

## Screens

The following screens must be reachable by URL. Other screens must be reachable through the UI.
Server-side and client-side rendering are both permitted.

| Route | Screen |
|---|---|
| `/` | The dossier list with search, and a form to research a domain |
| `/dossiers/{domain}` | One dossier: its state, its six fields with their values, status and citations, a refresh and a reload |
| `/dossiers/{domain}/evidence` | Every candidate of every field of that dossier |
| `/contested` | Every contested field across all dossiers |
| `/signup` | Signup |
| `/login` | Login |

The browser and the API share `/dossiers/{domain}`. Return the UI for `Accept: text/html`;
API requests without that header receive JSON. `/`, `/dossiers/{domain}/evidence` and
`/contested` are browser routes; they read the API's dossier data. The domain in a browser
route is normalised as in §4.

The UI must expose the `data-testid` attributes listed below for integration testing. Additional
elements are permitted, and the visual implementation is the team's choice subject to the
product-quality requirements below.

## Product and visual direction

The browser experience must feel like a coherent, presentation-ready research product, not a
thin wrapper of raw controls. Aim for a calm, legible, evidence-first character: a reader
opening a dossier should see at a glance which fields are known, which are unknown and which
are contested, and where each value came from.

A field's value and its status must be the clearest information on the dossier screen, with
its citations directly beside it. Fields, citations, candidates and contested fields should be
easy to scan, and status, provider, page kind and publication time should be understandable
without interpreting raw API data. Use a consistent visual system for typography, spacing,
colour, controls and feedback. Primary actions — research, refresh — must be easy to identify.
Known, unknown, contested, building, failed, loading, successful, refused and uncertain states
must be visually distinct as well as satisfying the behavioural requirements below. Format
names, years, headcount ranges, money and timestamps for people first; expose technical
identifiers only where they help the user. Each citation shows its excerpt as quoted text and
links to its URL.

The required flows must remain clear and usable at a 375 CSS-pixel viewport and at conventional
desktop widths, without horizontal page scrolling. Inputs need visible labels, keyboard focus must
be apparent, and text and controls need sufficient contrast. Provide considered empty, loading and
error states, and keep navigation consistent across the required routes. A custom illustration,
brand asset or exact visual match to a reference is not required.

## Signup and login

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `signup-email`, `signup-password`, `signup-display-name` | Inputs |
| `signup-submit` | Button |

The stage-1 requirements continue to apply, with the additions below. Numbered section
references such as §4 and §7 refer to `stage-1.md`.

selects one per field by a fixed rule. Researchers read dossiers, their evidence and the
fields in dispute in a browser.

3. A field's selected value is the one the selection rule below picks from the field's

## Page kind and publication time

Two header lines (§4, Pages) now carry requirements:

| Header line | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Kind: own`, `Kind: filing`, `Kind: news`, `Kind: aggregator` | The page's **kind**: the company's own site, a filing registry, a news report, or an aggregator of company data |
| `Published: <RFC 3339 timestamp>` | When the page was published |

A page with no `Kind` line, or with a value not listed above, is of kind `own` when the
host of its URL, normalised as `stage-1.md` normalises a domain, is the company's domain,
and of kind `aggregator` otherwise. A page with no `Published` line, or with a value that is not an RFC 3339 timestamp, has no
publication time.

## Page text

From this stage, a page's **text** is the text a browser shows once the page has loaded,
without clicking controls. Activating disclosure controls is not required. The graded
corpus contains no facts that require a click to reveal them.
Evidence (§4) is read from page text so defined, and a citation's excerpt must appear in the
page's text. A citation's `provider` is the provider that served the text the excerpt was
copied from.

## Web access

From this stage an extract through `nimble` may ask Nimble to load the page in a browser and
serve the text the browser shows once the page has loaded, with no control activated:
`provider_options={"render": True}` on WebRouter's extract.

Two optional browser vendors are also available, in addition to the providers in §2:

- `kernel`, through `open_browser`;
- `browserbase`, through `open_browser` and `browse`.

A service may use Nimble's rendered extract alone to obtain every page's browser text;
neither browser vendor is required.

The deployment provides these environment variables in addition to those in §2:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `KERNEL_API_KEY` | Credential for the `kernel` provider |
| `KERNEL_BASE_URL` | Base URL of the `kernel` provider endpoint |
| `BROWSERBASE_API_KEY` | Credential for the `browserbase` provider |
| `BROWSERBASE_BASE_URL` | Base URL of the `browserbase` provider endpoint |

WebRouter reads the keys from the environment. A service that uses these vendors passes their
base URLs to WebRouter in `provider_config`, beside those of §2:

```python
provider_config={"kernel": {"base_url": <KERNEL_BASE_URL>},
                 "browserbase": {"base_url": <BROWSERBASE_BASE_URL>}}
```

These calls cost, in the units of §9:

| Call | Cost |
|---|---|
| Extract through `nimble` that loads the page in a browser | 3 per URL requested, including a URL for which no page is returned |
| Open a session through `kernel` | 0 |
| Open a session through `browserbase` | 2 |
| Each page served to a session, through either | 1 |
| Browse run through `browserbase` | 4 |

A failed open, a failed page load and releasing a session cost nothing.

Each provider keeps at most 4 sessions open at once; opening another is answered with an
error. A session that no client has been connected to for 60 seconds is closed by the
provider.

From this stage a provider may answer any call with 429. A call answered 429 costs nothing
(`stage-1.md` §9). The same call (the same provider, operation and arguments) made again less
than one second after a 429 for it was answered is answered 429 again. No call is answered
429 more than three times in a row, except that opening a session while its provider keeps
4 open (Web access) is answered 429 until one of them closes. Time a build spends waiting to
make a call again after a 429 does not count toward the 10 seconds of `stage-1.md` §8.

value that a page of the evidence (§4) supports for a field is a candidate of that field,
once for each such page. The evidence now also holds the page that each research claim of
the evidence cites, whether or not the citation supports its claim: a build reads that page

candidate. A candidate's `provider` is a provider that served the text
its excerpt is taken from; when several did, any of them may be given.

```json
{
  "value": "Dana Ruiz",
  "status": "contested",
  "citations": [ { "url": "https://acme-robotics.test/about", "excerpt": "...", "provider": "nimble" } ],
  "candidates": [
    { "value": "Dana Ruiz", "url": "https://acme-robotics.test/about",
      "excerpt": "Dana Ruiz has led Acme Robotics as chief executive since 2021.",
      "provider": "nimble", "kind": "own",
      "published_at": "2026-01-10T00:00:00+00:00",
      "retrieved_at": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00", "selected": true },
    { "value": "Sam Ortiz", "url": "https://bizdata.test/acme-robotics",
      "excerpt": "Acme Robotics CEO: Sam Ortiz.",
      "provider": "tavily", "kind": "aggregator",
      "published_at": "2026-02-20T00:00:00+00:00",
      "retrieved_at": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00", "selected": false }
  ]
}
```

- `url`, `excerpt` and `provider` follow the citation rules in §4.
- `kind` is the page's kind, and `published_at` its publication time or null. Only an
  imported candidate (below) has a null `kind`; it has the authority of `aggregator`.
- `retrieved_at` is the time of the build that gathered the candidate (§8, Builds).
- `selected` is true on exactly one candidate of a field that has candidates, the one the
  rule picks, and false on the others.
- `candidates` lists the candidates of the last build that completed `ready`, in the order
  the selection rule ranks them, the selected one first. A field with no candidate has
  `"candidates": []` and is `unknown`.
- Two values are the same value when they are equal as JSON values; strings are compared
  exactly, after removing surrounding whitespace.

## The selection rule

Rank a field's candidates, highest first, by:

1. **Authority** of the page's kind: `own` and `filing` rank equal and highest, then `news`,
   then `aggregator`.
2. **Recency** within the same authority: the later `published_at` ranks higher. A candidate
   without a publication time ranks below every candidate of the same authority that has one.
3. **URL**: when authority and publication time are equal, the candidate whose `url` is
   smaller, comparing the strings by Unicode code point, ranks higher; between two
   candidates with the same URL, they rank by provider in the order `nimble`, `tavily`,
   `kernel`, `browserbase`.
4. **Value**: between two candidates with the same URL and provider, the one whose value is
   smaller ranks higher: integers compare as numbers, strings by Unicode code point after
   removing surrounding whitespace.

The highest-ranked candidate is the selected one. The field's `value` is the selected
candidate's value, and its `citations` are the `url`, `excerpt` and `provider` of every
candidate with that value, in rank order.

A candidate of lower authority is selected only when no candidate of higher authority
exists for that field. The rule runs over all of a field's candidates.

links to its URL.

desktop widths, without horizontal page scrolling. Inputs need visible labels, keyboard focus must

The stage-1 requirements continue to apply, with the additions below. Numbered section
references such as §4 and §7 refer to `stage-1.md`.

Sources disagree. A dossier now keeps every value its evidence supports, as candidates, and
selects one per field by a fixed rule. Researchers read dossiers, their evidence and the
fields in dispute in a browser.

The following applies to all operations, in addition to the stage-1 list:

3. A field's selected value is the one the selection rule below picks from the field's

## Page kind and publication time

Two header lines (§4, Pages) now carry requirements:

| Header line | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Kind: own`, `Kind: filing`, `Kind: news`, `Kind: aggregator` | The page's **kind**: the company's own site, a filing registry, a news report, or an aggregator of company data |
| `Published: <RFC 3339 timestamp>` | When the page was published |

A page with no `Kind` line, or with a value not listed above, is of kind `own` when the
host of its URL, normalised as `stage-1.md` normalises a domain, is the company's domain,
and of kind `aggregator` otherwise. A page with no `Published` line, or with a value that is not an RFC 3339 timestamp, has no
publication time.

## Page text

From this stage, a page's **text** is the text a browser shows once the page has loaded,
without clicking controls. Activating disclosure controls is not required. The graded
corpus contains no facts that require a click to reveal them.
Evidence (§4) is read from page text so defined, and a citation's excerpt must appear in the
page's text. A citation's `provider` is the provider that served the text the excerpt was
copied from.

## Web access

From this stage an extract through `nimble` may ask Nimble to load the page in a browser and
serve the text the browser shows once the page has loaded, with no control activated:
`provider_options={"render": True}` on WebRouter's extract.

Two optional browser vendors are also available, in addition to the providers in §2:

- `kernel`, through `open_browser`;
- `browserbase`, through `open_browser` and `browse`.

A service may use Nimble's rendered extract alone to obtain every page's browser text;
neither browser vendor is required.

The deployment provides these environment variables in addition to those in §2:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `KERNEL_API_KEY` | Credential for the `kernel` provider |
| `KERNEL_BASE_URL` | Base URL of the `kernel` provider endpoint |
| `BROWSERBASE_API_KEY` | Credential for the `browserbase` provider |
| `BROWSERBASE_BASE_URL` | Base URL of the `browserbase` provider endpoint |

WebRouter reads the keys from the environment. A service that uses these vendors passes their
base URLs to WebRouter in `provider_config`, beside those of §2:

```python
provider_config={"kernel": {"base_url": <KERNEL_BASE_URL>},
                 "browserbase": {"base_url": <BROWSERBASE_BASE_URL>}}
```

These calls cost, in the units of §9:

| Call | Cost |
|---|---|
| Extract through `nimble` that loads the page in a browser | 3 per URL requested, including a URL for which no page is returned |
| Open a session through `kernel` | 0 |
| Open a session through `browserbase` | 2 |
| Each page served to a session, through either | 1 |
| Browse run through `browserbase` | 4 |

A failed open, a failed page load and releasing a session cost nothing.

Each provider keeps at most 4 sessions open at once; opening another is answered with an
error. A session that no client has been connected to for 60 seconds is closed by the
provider.

## Rate limits

From this stage a provider may answer any call with 429. A call answered 429 costs nothing
(`stage-1.md` §9). The same call (the same provider, operation and arguments) made again less
than one second after a 429 for it was answered is answered 429 again. No call is answered
429 more than three times in a row, except that opening a session while its provider keeps
4 open (Web access) is answered 429 until one of them closes. Time a build spends waiting to
make a call again after a 429 does not count toward the 10 seconds of `stage-1.md` §8.

## Candidates

A **candidate** is one value for one field, supported by one excerpt of one page. Every
value that a page of the evidence (§4) supports for a field is a candidate of that field,
once for each such page. The evidence now also holds the page that each research claim of
the evidence cites, whether or not the citation supports its claim: a build reads that page
as it reads any other. A research claim whose citation does not support it is still not a
candidate. A candidate's `provider` is a provider that served the text
its excerpt is taken from; when several did, any of them may be given.

Each field gains `candidates`:

```json
{
  "value": "Dana Ruiz",
  "status": "contested",
  "citations": [ { "url": "https://acme-robotics.test/about", "excerpt": "...", "provider": "nimble" } ],
  "candidates": [
    { "value": "Dana Ruiz", "url": "https://acme-robotics.test/about",
      "excerpt": "Dana Ruiz has led Acme Robotics as chief executive since 2021.",
      "provider": "nimble", "kind": "own",
      "published_at": "2026-01-10T00:00:00+00:00",
      "retrieved_at": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00", "selected": true },
    { "value": "Sam Ortiz", "url": "https://bizdata.test/acme-robotics",
      "excerpt": "Acme Robotics CEO: Sam Ortiz.",
      "provider": "tavily", "kind": "aggregator",
      "published_at": "2026-02-20T00:00:00+00:00",
      "retrieved_at": "2026-03-01T09:00:00+00:00", "selected": false }
  ]
}
```

- `url`, `excerpt` and `provider` follow the citation rules in §4.
- `kind` is the page's kind, and `published_at` its publication time or null. Only an
  imported candidate (below) has a null `kind`; it has the authority of `aggregator`.
- `retrieved_at` is the time of the build that gathered the candidate (§8, Builds).
- `selected` is true on exactly one candidate of a field that has candidates, the one the
  rule picks, and false on the others.
- `candidates` lists the candidates of the last build that completed `ready`, in the order
  the selection rule ranks them, the selected one first. A field with no candidate has
  `"candidates": []` and is `unknown`.
- Two values are the same value when they are equal as JSON values; strings are compared
  exactly, after removing surrounding whitespace.

## The selection rule

Rank a field's candidates, highest first, by:

1. **Authority** of the page's kind: `own` and `filing` rank equal and highest, then `news`,
   then `aggregator`.
2. **Recency** within the same authority: the later `published_at` ranks higher. A candidate
   without a publication time ranks below every candidate of the same authority that has one.
3. **URL**: when authority and publication time are equal, the candidate whose `url` is
   smaller, comparing the strings by Unicode code point, ranks higher; between two
   candidates with the same URL, they rank by provider in the order `nimble`, `tavily`,
   `kernel`, `browserbase`.
4. **Value**: between two candidates with the same URL and provider, the one whose value is
   smaller ranks higher: integers compare as numbers, strings by Unicode code point after
   removing surrounding whitespace.

The highest-ranked candidate is the selected one. The field's `value` is the selected
candidate's value, and its `citations` are the `url`, `excerpt` and `provider` of every
candidate with that value, in rank order.

A candidate of lower authority is selected only when no candidate of higher authority
exists for that field. The rule runs over all of a field's candidates.

## Status

`status` is now one of three values:

| `status` | When |
|---|---|
| `known` | The field has candidates, and they all have the same value |
| `contested` | The field's candidates carry two or more different values |
| `unknown` | The field has no candidate; `value` is null |

A `contested` field still has a selected `value` and its citations.

`GET /dossiers` (§8) is unchanged. The `legal_name` it lists is the selected value.

## Screens

The following screens must be reachable by URL. Other screens must be reachable through the UI.
Server-side and client-side rendering are both permitted.

| Route | Screen |
|---|---|
| `/` | The dossier list with search, and a form to research a domain |
| `/dossiers/{domain}` | One dossier: its state, its six fields with their values, status and citations, a refresh and a reload |
| `/dossiers/{domain}/evidence` | Every candidate of every field of that dossier |
| `/contested` | Every contested field across all dossiers |
| `/signup` | Signup |
| `/login` | Login |

The browser and the API share `/dossiers/{domain}`. Return the UI for `Accept: text/html`;
API requests without that header receive JSON. `/`, `/dossiers/{domain}/evidence` and
`/contested` are browser routes; they read the API's dossier data. The domain in a browser
route is normalised as in §4.

The UI must expose the `data-testid` attributes listed below for integration testing. Additional
elements are permitted, and the visual implementation is the team's choice subject to the
product-quality requirements below.

## Product and visual direction

The browser experience must feel like a coherent, presentation-ready research product, not a
thin wrapper of raw controls. Aim for a calm, legible, evidence-first character: a reader
opening a dossier should see at a glance which fields are known, which are unknown and which
are contested, and where each value came from.

A field's value and its status must be the clearest information on the dossier screen, with
its citations directly beside it. Fields, citations, candidates and contested fields should be
easy to scan, and status, provider, page kind and publication time should be understandable
without interpreting raw API data. Use a consistent visual system for typography, spacing,
colour, controls and feedback. Primary actions — research, refresh — must be easy to identify.
Known, unknown, contested, building, failed, loading, successful, refused and uncertain states
must be visually distinct as well as satisfying the behavioural requirements below. Format
names, years, headcount ranges, money and timestamps for people first; expose technical
identifiers only where they help the user. Each citation shows its excerpt as quoted text and
links to its URL.

The required flows must remain clear and usable at a 375 CSS-pixel viewport and at conventional
desktop widths, without horizontal page scrolling. Inputs need visible labels, keyboard focus must
be apparent, and text and controls need sufficient contrast. Provide considered empty, loading and
error states, and keep navigation consistent across the required routes. A custom illustration,
brand asset or exact visual match to a reference is not required.

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|

## Dossier — `/dossiers/{domain}`

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `dossier-domain` | Text is exactly the normalised domain |
| `dossier-state` | Text is exactly `building`, `ready` or `failed` |
| `dossier-spent` | Formatted `spent_units`. Carries `data-units="{integer}"` |

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|

## Contested fields — `/contested`

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `contested-list` | Container. Children ordered by domain ascending, then by field in the order of the table in `stage-1.md` §4 |
| `contested-item-{domain}-{field}` | One per contested field of any dossier. Carries `data-value` for the selected value. Text contains the domain, the field and every distinct candidate value. Links to `/dossiers/{domain}/evidence` |
| `empty-contested` | Shown instead of the list when no field is contested |

## Refresh and competing clients

After any successful action, the data on the same page must show the new state without a manual
reload. Navigation must wait for the write to succeed before it refreshes the data. Any mechanism
is fine, including a full navigation. Apart from the reading while a dossier is `building`,
there is no live-update requirement: another client may change state, but this browser need
only read again after its own action, an explicit reload or a build it is waiting on.

- `dossier-reload` reads the dossier again. **Latest read wins:** a delayed earlier read must
  not overwrite a later one, including when responses arrive out of order. This applies to the
  reads while a dossier is `building` as well.
- Another client may refresh a dossier after this browser reads it. A refresh from this
  browser while that build runs is answered 202 like any other and the screen follows the
  running build to its end.
- If a research or refresh response is lost, including after the request commits, show
  `research-uncertain` or `refresh-uncertain` (nonempty text), not `research-error` or
  `refresh-error`. Keep the request retryable with the **same key and body**. A successful
  retry removes both the error and the uncertainty elements, shows the dossier, and starts at
  most one build. Unknown outcomes are not confirmed refusals.

No background polling beyond the reading while `building`, live synchronization, or recovery
across page reloads is required.

## Existing clients after an upgrade

A stage-2 service must accept an export produced by the same team's stage-1 service. A browser
signed in before that export/import upgrade must remain signed in afterwards. Imported dossiers
appear in the list and on their screens. Each imported field gains one candidate for every
value that text the providers served to the dossier's last stage-1 build that completed
`ready` supports for that field (`stage-1.md` §4), once for each page whose served text
supports it. The candidate's excerpt is taken from that text and supports the value; its
`provider` is the provider that served that text, its `kind` and `published_at` are as the
exported state records them or else null, and its `retrieved_at` is the dossier's
`researched_at`. Each imported field's `value`, `status` and `citations` then follow from its
candidates by the selection rule and Status, as after a build. A research or refresh
request whose response was lost before export remains retryable after import with the same body and key; the UI must recover the original response
and show the imported dossier. These requirements apply when import completes between browser
requests; migration during an in-flight request is not required. No page reload or new screen
is required.

The candidates of an imported dossier are replaced by those of its next completed build.

`status` is now one of three values:

| `status` | When |
|---|---|
| `known` | The field has candidates, and they all have the same value |
| `contested` | The field's candidates carry two or more different values |
| `unknown` | The field has no candidate; `value` is null |

A `contested` field still has a selected `value` and its citations.

`GET /dossiers` (§8) is unchanged. The `legal_name` it lists is the selected value.

## Screens

The following screens must be reachable by URL. Other screens must be reachable through the UI.
Server-side and client-side rendering are both permitted.

| Route | Screen |
|---|---|
| `/` | The dossier list with search, and a form to research a domain |
| `/dossiers/{domain}` | One dossier: its state, its six fields with their values, status and citations, a refresh and a reload |
| `/dossiers/{domain}/evidence` | Every candidate of every field of that dossier |
| `/contested` | Every contested field across all dossiers |
| `/signup` | Signup |
| `/login` | Login |

The browser and the API share `/dossiers/{domain}`. Return the UI for `Accept: text/html`;
API requests without that header receive JSON. `/`, `/dossiers/{domain}/evidence` and
`/contested` are browser routes; they read the API's dossier data. The domain in a browser
route is normalised as in §4.

The UI must expose the `data-testid` attributes listed below for integration testing. Additional
elements are permitted, and the visual implementation is the team's choice subject to the
product-quality requirements below.

## Product and visual direction

The browser experience must feel like a coherent, presentation-ready research product, not a
thin wrapper of raw controls. Aim for a calm, legible, evidence-first character: a reader
opening a dossier should see at a glance which fields are known, which are unknown and which
are contested, and where each value came from.

A field's value and its status must be the clearest information on the dossier screen, with
its citations directly beside it. Fields, citations, candidates and contested fields should be
easy to scan, and status, provider, page kind and publication time should be understandable
without interpreting raw API data. Use a consistent visual system for typography, spacing,
colour, controls and feedback. Primary actions — research, refresh — must be easy to identify.
Known, unknown, contested, building, failed, loading, successful, refused and uncertain states
must be visually distinct as well as satisfying the behavioural requirements below. Format
names, years, headcount ranges, money and timestamps for people first; expose technical
identifiers only where they help the user. Each citation shows its excerpt as quoted text and
links to its URL.

The required flows must remain clear and usable at a 375 CSS-pixel viewport and at conventional
desktop widths, without horizontal page scrolling. Inputs need visible labels, keyboard focus must
be apparent, and text and controls need sufficient contrast. Provide considered empty, loading and
error states, and keep navigation consistent across the required routes. A custom illustration,
brand asset or exact visual match to a reference is not required.

## Signup and login

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `signup-email`, `signup-password`, `signup-display-name` | Inputs |
| `signup-submit` | Button |
| `login-email`, `login-password`, `login-submit` | Inputs and button |
| `auth-error` | Error message. Present only when there is one |
| `current-user` | Visible on every screen when signed in. Text contains the display name |
| `logout-button` | Button |

## Dossier list — `/`

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `research-domain` | Input for the domain to research |
| `research-submit` | Button. Sends `POST /dossiers` |
| `research-error` | Error message, when the request is refused — including an invalid domain |
| `research-uncertain` | Shown when the outcome of a research request is unknown (below) |
| `dossier-search` | Input. Filters the list as `q` does on `GET /dossiers` |
| `dossier-list` | Container. Children ordered by domain ascending |
| `dossier-item-{domain}` | One per listed dossier. Carries `data-state="{state}"`. Text contains the domain, and the legal name when known. Links to `/dossiers/{domain}` |
| `empty-dossiers` | Shown instead of the list when no dossier matches |

A research request that succeeds, with 202 or 200, opens `/dossiers/{domain}` for the
normalised domain. A domain that already has a dossier, including one created by another
client after this browser read the list, opens that dossier and starts no build.

## Dossier — `/dossiers/{domain}`

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `dossier-domain` | Text is exactly the normalised domain |
| `dossier-state` | Text is exactly `building`, `ready` or `failed` |
| `dossier-spent` | Formatted `spent_units`. Carries `data-units="{integer}"` |
| `dossier-researched-at` | Text contains `researched_at`, formatted. Absent when it is null |
| `field-{field}` | One per field, six in all, in the order of the table in `stage-1.md` §4. Carries `data-status="{status}"` |
| `field-value-{field}` | The formatted value. Carries `data-value` (below). Present only when the value is not null |
| `field-contested-{field}` | A marker. Present only when the field is `contested` |
| `field-citations-{field}` | Container of the field's citations, in API order |
| `citation-{field}-{n}` | The field's `n`th citation, counting from 1. Text contains the excerpt. Contains a link whose `href` is the citation's `url`. Carries `data-provider="{provider}"` |
| `dossier-evidence-link` | Link to `/dossiers/{domain}/evidence` |
| `dossier-refresh` | Button. Sends `POST /dossiers/{domain}/refresh` |
| `refresh-error` | Error message, when a refresh is refused |
| `refresh-uncertain` | Shown when the outcome of a refresh is unknown (below) |
| `dossier-reload` | Button. Reads the dossier again without starting a build |
| `dossier-not-found` | Shown instead of the fields when no dossier exists for the domain |

`data-value` is the API value as text: a string value unchanged, an integer in plain decimal
digits.

While the dossier's state is `building`, the screen reads the dossier again at least every
2 seconds until the state is `ready` or `failed`, and then shows the new fields without a
manual reload.

## Evidence — `/dossiers/{domain}/evidence`

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `evidence-{field}` | One container per field, six in all. Children in API `candidates` order |
| `candidate-{field}-{n}` | The field's `n`th candidate, counting from 1. Text contains the formatted value and the excerpt. Carries `data-value`, `data-provider`, `data-kind`, `data-url`, `data-published-at` (the RFC 3339 `published_at`, empty when null) and `data-selected="true"` or `"false"` |
| `evidence-empty-{field}` | Shown instead of candidates when the field has none |

## Contested fields — `/contested`

| `data-testid` | Element |
|---|---|
| `contested-list` | Container. Children ordered by domain ascending, then by field in the order of the table in `stage-1.md` §4 |
| `contested-item-{domain}-{field}` | One per contested field of any dossier. Carries `data-value` for the selected value. Text contains the domain, the field and every distinct candidate value. Links to `/dossiers/{domain}/evidence` |
| `empty-contested` | Shown instead of the list when no field is contested |

## Refresh and competing clients

After any successful action, the data on the same page must show the new state without a manual
reload. Navigation must wait for the write to succeed before it refreshes the data. Any mechanism
is fine, including a full navigation. Apart from the reading while a dossier is `building`,
there is no live-update requirement: another client may change state, but this browser need
only read again after its own action, an explicit reload or a build it is waiting on.

- `dossier-reload` reads the dossier again. **Latest read wins:** a delayed earlier read must
  not overwrite a later one, including when responses arrive out of order. This applies to the
  reads while a dossier is `building` as well.
- Another client may refresh a dossier after this browser reads it. A refresh from this
  browser while that build runs is answered 202 like any other and the screen follows the
  running build to its end.
- If a research or refresh response is lost, including after the request commits, show
  `research-uncertain` or `refresh-uncertain` (nonempty text), not `research-error` or
  `refresh-error`. Keep the request retryable with the **same key and body**. A successful
  retry removes both the error and the uncertainty elements, shows the dossier, and starts at
  most one build. Unknown outcomes are not confirmed refusals.

No background polling beyond the reading while `building`, live synchronization, or recovery
across page reloads is required.

## Existing clients after an upgrade

A stage-2 service must accept an export produced by the same team's stage-1 service. A browser
signed in before that export/import upgrade must remain signed in afterwards. Imported dossiers
appear in the list and on their screens. Each imported field gains one candidate for every
value that text the providers served to the dossier's last stage-1 build that completed
`ready` supports for that field (`stage-1.md` §4), once for each page whose served text
supports it. The candidate's excerpt is taken from that text and supports the value; its
`provider` is the provider that served that text, its `kind` and `published_at` are as the
exported state records them or else null, and its `retrieved_at` is the dossier's
`researched_at`. Each imported field's `value`, `status` and `citations` then follow from its
candidates by the selection rule and Status, as after a build. A research or refresh
request whose response was lost before export remains retryable after import with the same body and key; the UI must recover the original response
and show the imported dossier. These requirements apply when import completes between browser
requests; migration during an in-flight request is not required. No page reload or new screen
is required.

The candidates of an imported dossier are replaced by those of its next completed build.
===== END SPECIFICATION =====

@[[8ea258b8-a8ca-45f0-9ebe-2714998424c7]] Reviewer: I read the full stage-2 spec from your message. I did not open the stage-1 spec file, the corpus, or any later stage, and I have not run anything yet. I'll run one harness check at a time into a new out dir, from a fresh clone of the reported commit.

Highest-risk areas I'll probe:
1. Selection rule. The order is authority (own = filing > news > aggregator), then later published_at, with a missing time ranked last. After that come URL by code point, provider order (nimble, tavily, kernel, browserbase), and value (integers as numbers, strings trimmed). I'll check that candidates are listed in rank order, that selected is true on exactly one, that value and citations come from the selected value, and that status is known, contested or unknown. I'll also check that an imported candidate with null kind ranks as aggregator.
2. Kind and Published defaults. A missing or unlisted Kind falls back to own or aggregator by the normalised (www-stripped) domain. A bad Published value gives null.
3. Candidates. There should be one per supporting page, including the page a research claim cites. A claim whose citation does not support it must not become a candidate. Excerpt must appear in the browser text, and provider must be the one that served that text. retrieved_at is the build time. candidates come from the last build that completed ready.
4. Browser-rendered text. Nimble render=True costs 3 per URL, including URLs with no page returned. I'll look at the cost budget with browser sessions (kernel 0, browserbase 2, 1 per page, 4 per browse), the 4-session cap, and session release and leaks. I'll check that no facts are read from unrendered text only.
5. 429 handling. A call answered 429 costs nothing. Retry must wait at least 1 second, up to 3 times in a row. Open-session 429 persists while 4 sessions are open. 429 wait time must not count toward the 10s build limit. I'll also look for double-billing on retries.
6. Spend and results ratio against the stage-1 revision on a fixed workload. Unneeded renders, or fetching every URL through every provider, count as a defect even if under the limit.
7. UI testids across all six routes. That means the data-* attributes, list ordering, and the Accept: text/html versus JSON negotiation on /dossiers/{domain}. Domain normalisation on browser routes. Not-found, empty and error states. current-user visible on every screen.
8. UI behaviour. Polling at least every 2s while building, with latest-read-wins under out-of-order responses (including during polling). Reload must not start a build. Research for an existing domain opens it and starts no build. Refresh while another client's build runs returns 202 and follows that build. Navigation waits for the write to succeed.
9. Lost-response handling. research-uncertain and refresh-uncertain, not the error elements. A retry with the same key and body clears both elements and starts at most one build.
10. Stage-1 to stage-2 upgrade. Import a stage-1 export. The session stays signed in. Imported fields get candidates re-derived from the last ready build's served text (retrieved_at = researched_at, kind and published_at from the export or null). Value, status and citations follow the rule. A lost-response retry with the old key and body still recovers the original response.
11. Stage-1 regressions. I'll run the carried-forward ledger and acceptance tests, plus the strict isolated mode (no outbound network) from a clean clone.
12. Overfitting and plausibility. I'll check that the code doesn't special-case fixture values. I'll read real outputs on the Analyst's realistic fixtures. I'll check formatting of names, years, money and timestamps. I'll check layout at 375px without horizontal scroll, labels and focus, and visually distinct states.

Send the review request with the repo path, commit and run instructions when ready.

**Requirements worked from:** the stage-2 spec pasted in your handoff, plus `stage-1.md` §4, §8, §9 and §10. I did not read the ledger or the acceptance tests.

**What it does**
- **Candidates and selection:** `evidence.py` reads each page's browser text and makes one candidate per field, page and value, with the page's kind and `Published` time. `selection.py` ranks them by authority, then recency, then URL, then provider, then value. It selects the first and derives `value`, `status` (known/contested/unknown) and `citations`. Kind and publication time follow the spec's header and fallback rules.
- **Rendered extract:** page text now comes only from the rendered Nimble extract (3 units a page). I tested this against the mock with WebRouter: plain and rendered text differ on some pages, so evidence read from search or plain-extract text would fail the "excerpt must appear in page text" rule. This is why the stage-1 builder was replaced.
- **Budget:** each build runs 7 lite searches (1 unit each) and 1 research run (25 units), then renders as many pages as the remaining budget buys, research-cited pages first. Builds against the sample mock spent 68 to 80 units.
- **429 handling:** a 429 is retried after 1.05 s, up to 3 times. The waiting is excluded from the build's time window. Under a permanent `rate_limit` fault a build took 6.6 s; under `throttle` it took 2.3 s. Both ended `ready` at 80 units.
- **Import:** a stage-1 export imports, and the fields are recomputed by the selection rule. A field with no `candidates` gets one candidate per citation, with null `kind` and `published_at` and `retrieved_at` set to `researched_at`. Tokens and idempotency records are kept, so a lost response is retryable after import. I tested this with a real export from the final stage-1 service: import returned 204, the fields showed candidates, and the same key replayed as 200.
- **UI:** all six routes with the listed `data-testid`s, served by `ui.py` and `static/` (no build step, no external assets). `/dossiers/{domain}` returns the UI for `Accept: text/html` and JSON otherwise. Details:
  - **Building and reads:** a building dossier is re-read every 1 s, and a stale read never overwrites a newer one.
  - **Lost responses:** a lost research or refresh response shows the `*-uncertain` element and is retried with the same key and body.
  - **Session and domain:** the bearer token is kept in `localStorage`, and the domain in the URL is normalised.
  - **Layout:** system font stack, no horizontal scroll at 375 px.

**Checks I ran**
- `/tmp/impl-venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests` from `stage-2/`: 36 tests pass (selection, evidence, store, import, UI routes).
- `docker build -q -t dossier-s2-impl stage-2` builds.
- A Playwright run at 375 px and 1280 px against the local mock covered:
  - Signup error, login, an invalid-domain research error, and a lost research response showing the uncertain element.
  - The retry then produced one domain search and one research run, with the state going building to ready.
  - The refresh uncertain-then-retry path, the not-found state, search, empty states, logout, and no horizontal scroll (scrollWidth 375 and 1280).
- Screenshots are in `/tmp/impl-scratch/shots/`.

**Known gaps**
- **Stage-1 import is limited.** A stage-1 export does not record the served page text. Imported candidates therefore come only from the cited excerpts, so values the served text would also support (a competing city, for example) are missing until the next build. This cannot be fixed in the final stage-1 folder.
- **Live-provider behaviour is untested.** I only ran against the mock. Kernel and Browserbase are not used.
- **Rendered-page budget:** a company with more than about 16 relevant pages, after the research run, leaves its lowest-ranked pages unread. Those pages are ranked by likelihood and are never read.
- **Judgment calls the spec leaves open:** money is shown as `$75,000,000` and headcount as `1001-5000 employees`, so the raw digits stay in the text. `data-kind` is empty for imported candidates.

I rejected 5a06057 for now, pending a ruling on the stage-1 import. I didn't run isolated mode, since I'm not accepting.

- **Harness:** stage 1 and stage 2 pass on 5a06057. Stage 3 fails, as expected for a later stage. The earlier run on a41b62a also passed stage 2.
- **Import (REJECT):** the stage-2 service builds candidates for imported dossiers only from the cited excerpts. The spec requires one for every value the served text supports. Three upgrade tests fail for that reason, for example bluefin-marine imports as `known` with 2005 only, where it should be `contested` with 2005 and 2008. The final stage-1 export carries no served text and stage-1 is final, so the coordinator has to rule on it. I think accepting the gap and changing the tests is the only workable option.
- **Test defects (Analyst):** two stage-1 tests still expect bluefin-marine to be `known`, which stage 2 makes `contested`. Three tests in `test_s2_api.py` fail with 401 only when the whole file runs, because a function-scope reset wipes the shared tokens. Run alone, they pass.
- **Spend:** every build in the suite spends 80 units, including no-trace, which gets 0 fields. I did not measure the stage-1 baseline, so I've asked the Implementer for stage-1 against stage-2 units per correct field.
- **headcount_range:** the Implementer's bucketing matches stage-1 §4, and the 5a06057 diff only adds a UI hint.

Not checked: a fresh clone and isolated mode, behaviour against live providers (429 handling), the UI suite (`test_s2_ui.py`, still untracked and being edited), and the 375 and 1280 layouts (no screenshots viewed).

- Harness on 5a06057, out dir checks/final-s2-s2-reviewer-2: stage 1 pass, stage 2 pass, stage 3 fail (later stage, expected). The same run on a41b62a (reviewer-1) gave stage 2 pass, 12 tests.

- I did not re-run run.sh on 5a06057. Its diff against a41b62a is UI-only (app.js and app.css).

1. REJECT, owner Coordinator for a ruling, then Implementer. The stage-1 import is incomplete (self-declared gap 1). I ran test_s2_upgrade.py with S1_DIR=stage-1: 5 passed, 3 failed.
   - Failures: test_every_imported_field_gains_a_candidate_for_each_supported_value_and_page[northwind-optics.test] and [bluefin-marine.test], and test_a_contested_dossier_imports_as_contested.
   - Example: bluefin-marine founded_year imports with one candidate, 2005. The stage-1 served text also supports 2008 from https://bizlistings-hub.test/bluefin-marine, so that candidate is missing. The field imports as known, where the spec requires contested.
   - northwind-optics is missing the Lisbon candidate from https://mirror-archive.test/northwind-optics/about.
   - This violates the spec sentence "a candidate for every value that text the providers served … supports … once for each page".
   - Cause: the final stage-1 export (store.py export_state) has no served page text, and stage-1 is FINAL.
   - Please rule on one of these:
     a. The stage-2 import re-fetches pages. It would need URLs it cannot learn from the export, so I think this is impossible.
     b. The gap is accepted as unavoidable. I think this is the only workable option, and the Analyst should then change those tests.
   - Please confirm that the whole suite, including the other upgrade tests, passes with the chosen ruling.
   - The tests that did pass cover the cited-excerpt candidates, null kind and published_at, retrieved_at = researched_at, and session and retry continuity.

2. Test and ledger defects, owner Analyst, not the Implementer:
   - test_builds.py::test_company_build_is_supported_and_within_budget[bluefin-marine.test] and test_contradicting_sources_hold_one_value_with_matching_citations still expect founded_year to be `known` with [2005, 2008]. Stage 2 makes it `contested`, with own 2005 selected over the aggregator's 2008, and the service output is correct. The stage-1 expectations need updating.
   - Three tests in test_s2_api.py (listed_legal_name, serves_json, normalises_its_domain) fail inside the full file with 401. A function-scope pworld reset wipes the tokens held by the module-scope s2 fixture. Run alone, all three pass. Fix the fixture isolation.

3. Spend against results. A build spends 80 units on every company in the suite. The known-fields-per-unit table shows 0.075 for 6/6-known companies, 0.025 to 0.05 for harbor-signal and kestrel-freight, and 0.000 for no-trace. The Implementer's own report says 68 to 80. Stage-2 spend is bounded, but there is no flat-versus-stage-1 comparison from me. I did not measure the stage-1 baseline per company. Implementer, please report stage-1 versus stage-2 units per correct field on the same workload.
   - Note that no-trace spends the full 80 units for 0 fields.

4. headcount_range. The Implementer's reading matches stage-1 §4. The valid values are `1-10`, `11-50`, `51-200`, `201-500`, `501-1000`, `1001-5000`, `5001-10000` and `10001+`, and the value is the range that contains the number. The 5a06057 diff only adds a UI hint ("The range that contains the headcount the sources state"). I did not find any bucketing change in the 5a06057 service code.

Not checked yet:
- Fresh clone and isolated mode.
- 429 and rate-limit behaviour against live providers.
- Visual plausibility at 375 and 1280 (I did not view screenshots).
- The UI suite test_s2_ui.py, which was still untracked and in flux.
- Kernel and browserbase, which are unused (gap 2, acceptable since the spec says Nimble render alone is allowed).

Re-review will be fast once the ruling and the test fixes land.

I committed a fix as `6b5b56699ff4c0875368647a9b3c9e66ef083a4f` and staged the reply to the coordinator. I re-ran the 37 unit tests (pass) but not the harness.

- **(A) Stage-1 import:** the gap is real and unavoidable. A stage-1 export holds no served text, search results, research claims or build records. The only URLs in it are the citation URLs. The import now turns each cited excerpt into a candidate for every field it supports, once per page and value. I imported a real 13-dossier stage-1 export and every selected value matched the stage-1 value. The bluefin-marine 2008 and northwind-optics Lisbon `test_s2_upgrade` failures remain, as ruled.
- **(B) Spend:** pages whose URL, title and snippet never name the company now get a 1-unit plain extract first. They are rendered only if that text names the company. On the same 13-domain workload:

| Build | Units | Known fields | Known per 100 units |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stage-1 | 384 | 69 | 18.0 |
| Stage-2 as rejected | 989 | 69 | 7.0 |
| Stage-2 now | 955 | 69 | 7.2 |

- **Unknown company:** the build with no trace went from 80 units to 46.
- **Candidates:** per-company candidate counts are equal or higher than before.
- **Why spend stays high:** only 30% of the pages found yield a candidate. Nearly all the rest mention the company but support no value, and telling them apart needs the 3-unit rendered text. Filtering further on plain text could drop candidates.
- **Residual risk:** a page that names the company only in script-injected text, and nowhere in its URL, title, snippet or plain text, would be skipped.

I stopped my local mock and both services.

@[[8ea258b8-a8ca-45f0-9ebe-2714998424c7]] New revision 6b5b56699ff4c0875368647a9b3c9e66ef083a4f (stage-2/). I verified the stage-1 export, so (A) is a real, unavoidable gap. Spend (B) is trimmed only where nothing supported is lost. I re-ran the 37 unit tests (pass) and did not re-run the harness. I did not touch `stage-2/requirements/`.

**(A) What a stage-1 export contains**
- **Contents:** I read `store.export_state` and a real export from the final stage-1 service. The top level is `track`, `format_version` and `state`. `state` holds only `users`, `tokens`, `dossiers`, `idempotency` and `dossier_counter`.
  - Each dossier has `dossier_id`, `domain`, `state`, `researched_at`, `spent_units` and `fields`, where each field is `value`, `status` and `citations`, and each citation is `url`, `excerpt` and `provider`.
  - Idempotency bodies are only `dossier_id`, `domain` and `state`.
- **What is missing:** there is no served text, search result, research claim, call log or build record. The only URLs in the whole export are the citation URLs (5 distinct URLs in my quillmate export). A page that stage-1 did not cite therefore leaves no trace to derive a candidate from. Fetching at import would break "import makes no provider call", so I did not.
- **What I added:** every cited excerpt is served text of a known page, so it now becomes a candidate for its own field and for any other field it supports. This is done once per page and value, with null `kind` and `published_at` and `retrieved_at` set to `researched_at`.
- **Imported values:** I imported a real stage-1 export of 13 dossiers into stage-2. 69 fields are known and 81 candidates were derived. Every selected value equals the stage-1 value.
- **Remaining failures:** the bluefin-marine 2008 and northwind-optics Lisbon `test_s2_upgrade` failures stay, per your ruling.

**(B) Spend, same 13-domain workload on the sample mock (12 companies plus one unknown domain)**

| Build | Units | Known fields | Known per 100 units | Candidates |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stage-1 | 384 | 69 | 18.0 | none |
| Stage-2, a41b62a (as rejected) | 989 | 69 | 7.0 | 97 |
| Stage-2, this revision | 955 | 69 | 7.2 | 98 |

- **Unknown company:** the build with no trace (`nosuchco.test`) went from 80 units to 46. Stage-1 spent 48.
- **Change:** a page whose URL, title and snippet never name the company is first checked with a plain extract (1 unit). It is rendered (3 units) only if the text it serves names the company. At most 30% of the budget left after discovery goes on these checks.
- **No candidate lost:** per-company candidate counts are equal or higher than before. larkspur-health gained one, because pages that used to be cut by the 80-unit cap are now reached.
- **Pages kept:** registry pages with no name in their URL or title still get rendered, because their text names the company.
- **Why the rest stays high:** I fetched all 232 pages found for the 13 domains. Only 70 of them (30%) yield a candidate. Of the rest, nearly all mention the company but support no value.
  - Telling these apart needs the browser text, and plain text differs from rendered text on some pages.
  - A plain-text filter on every page could drop a candidate, so I did not add one. The remaining spend is the 3-unit render of company-naming pages.
- **Residual risk:** a page that never names the company in its URL, title, snippet or served plain text, but names it only in script-injected text, would be skipped.
- **Unchanged:** the research run (25 units) always runs. It is the only way to reach pages that no search returns.

**Rulings that change behaviour (RULINGS 30–55):**
- **Exact selection.** Tests assert exact candidate order, selected value and status from the corpus, using the stage-1 oracle and the independent selection-rule model. Fragment-only candidates are tolerated but never required.
- **One candidate per (page, value).**
- **Browser text.** A page's `text` is what a browser shows; `static_text` is the stale served text. The build must read pages through Nimble's rendered extract (3 per URL) or a browser vendor, and a research-cited page that is not searchable must be read.
- **Kind and `Published`.**
  - An unlisted `Kind` falls back to the host rule: `www.` is stripped and `blog.<domain>` is another host.
  - A date-only value, a time with no offset, an impossible date such as Feb 30, or words give no publication time.

- **429 handling.**
  - A build must retry a refused call and end `ready` with the right candidates (tavily down; nimble throttled or permanently rate-limited).
  - Refused calls cost 0.
  - `throttle` mode has a time bound of 10 s plus 3 s per refusal plus 2 s.

  - Candidates come only from what the stage-1 export records.

  - Tokens and logins must survive, and replays of the same key and body must return the original response with no provider call.
  - Uncited pages (bluefin 2008, northwind mirror Lisbon) and contested-on-import are not required.
  - The UI half does a stage-2 export-then-import round trip with no page reload, plus a lost request recovered after import.
- **Latest read wins.** The test holds a read response back, lets a later read finish, then releases the old one. It falls back to a sequential check if the UI disables reload while a read is pending or reads serially.
- **Product-quality checks are heuristics.** They cover no horizontal scroll at 375 and 1280 px, WCAG AA contrast from computed colours, a visible focus indicator, visible labels, distinct computed colours for field statuses, dossier states and refused vs uncertain, a quoted citation with an exact-URL link, and no raw ISO timestamps or "null" on screen. I rejected 6b5b566. The shipped harness passes, but one Analyst test fails on a real code regression, owned by the Implementer. I didn't run isolated mode or a fresh clone, since I'm not accepting.

- **Harness:** stage 1 and stage 2 pass; stage 3 fails, as expected for a later stage.

- **Cause:** `config.py` stops starting new provider calls after 6 s of build time on any non-live host, and it is identical to stage-1's. Stage 2 makes more sequential rounds of calls, so with 3 s per call the second round never starts. The fix is to run each round's calls in parallel or overlap the rounds, not to widen the window.
- **Spend:** acceptable. The Analyst suite shows 46 to 64 units per build against the limit of 80, and the Implementer's 13-domain workload averages 73. It finds the same 69 known fields as stage 1 (7.2 per 100 units against 18.0), but the extra spend is mostly the 3-per-page render charge. Only 70 of 232 fetched pages yielded a candidate, so skipping pages with no company-fact signal would help. I have no cheaper design that keeps the full candidate set, so I did not reject on spend.

**Cause:** the plain-extract check added in 6b5b566 was a second sequential round after discovery. With every provider call delayed 3 s the rounds ran at 0, 3 and 6 s, and the 6 s gathering window closed before the rendering round. The build ended `ready` with every field unknown.

**Fix:** `Gateway.time_is_short()` is true once a build has used a third of its own `gather_window`. In that case the builder skips the plain-extract check and renders every page found. I did not widen the window or key anything on the mock host. In live mode the same rule scales to 66 s of 200 s.

**Trade-off:** under slow providers a build may spend units rendering pages that never name the company, but no candidate is lost. With fast providers behaviour is unchanged, and the 1-unit check is kept.
